one_month_reasoning: No Salesforce earnings in the window (Q3 FY27 due early December 2026). In-window: final ASR settlement (~34M more shares at the ~$182 expected average; known and mechanical), the Fin close (Contentful already closed 2026-09-01; both in guidance), peer prints (ServiceNow ~Oct 21-22, Microsoft/Dynamics ~Oct 28-29) and the FOMC. Oracle's September print (cloud apps +10%, Fusion +14%) was a mild positive read-across for enterprise application demand, but Microsoft flagged CRM bookings moderating in July, so peer read-across could cut either way. The stock is ~14% below its Sep-3 intraday high ($268.27) and bounced from $225.31 to $231.31 on 9/30; no clear drift signal. I use a near-symmetric distribution centred ~$232 with ~12.5-13% monthly sigma (47%/3.5) and slightly fat tails.

fair_value.method: Blend of forward P/E (14.5x NTM core EPS ~$17.4 = $252), SBC-adjusted FCF yield (NTM FCF ~$16.9B less SBC ~$4.7B at ~8.7-9% of revenue = $12.2B / ~787M shares at a 6.2% yield = $250) and EV/NTM sales (4.2x ~$54B = $227B less ~$29B net debt / 787M = $251); weights 40/35/25 give ~$251.

Between consensus ~$16.0 and a build of core FY27 net income ~$11.5B +~11% over ~785M shares (~$16.3); interest on the ASR notes already in the Q2 run-rate.
FY28 grown ~11%: ~9-10% revenue growth (organic ~7-8% plus Contentful/Fin), flat-to-slightly-up margin, and only ongoing net buybacks (~1-1.5%); the ASR benefit is not counted again.

Stock ~14.3x FY28 consensus today; trimmed from my round-1 15x because the Q3 guide implies only ~7-8% organic growth and peers (HubSpot, ServiceNow) are moving pricing toward meters; Oracle apps +10% shows enterprise app demand intact, so no de-rating either.
FY27 ~$15.3B grown ~7% to FY28 ~$16.4B and ~7% to FY29 ~$17.5B; NTM = 1/3 FY28 + 2/3 FY29 (≈$17.1B), trimmed for acquired-company cash burn.
FY27 margin bridge shows SBC at 9.0% of revenue (~$4.2B, $4.96/share); applied ~8.7% to NTM revenue ~$54B. Round 1 used ~$3.3B/7%, which was wrong.

~16x owner FCF for ~9-10% total growth with ~7-8% organic; a bit richer than a 6.4-6.5% yield because FCF conversion is high and buybacks continue, but below the large-cap software median given seat-pricing risk flagged by peers.

methods.name: EV/sales
methods.inputs: NTM revenue ~$54B x 4.2x = ~$227B EV, less ~$29B net debt, /787M shares

inputs_detail.derivation: FY28 ~$50.9B (+10% incl. Contentful/Fin) and FY29 ~$55.5B (+9%); NTM = 1/3 + 2/3 blend. The $63B FY30 target includes Informatica and announced M&A, so it is not treated as organic evidence.
Today: ~$182B market cap (787M x $231) + ~$33B net debt incl. deal cash = ~$215B, ~4.3x NTM sales; trimmed to 4.2x because an increasing share of revenue growth is acquired.
$27.9B at Jul-2026 plus ~$5.1B cash for Contentful ($1.5B, closed Sep-1) and Fin ($3.6B) = ~$33B, less ~$4B of FCF retained after dividends and ongoing buybacks. Anthropic stake not added.

bear.story: Peer evidence of seat compression spreads (Microsoft CRM bookings moderating, HubSpot/ServiceNow shift to metered/outcome pricing); the December print shows organic growth stuck at ~7% or lower with cRPO below guide, Agentforce ARR (widened definition) fails to offset, and leadership turnover in engineering (President/Chief Engineering Officer departed Aug-2026) slows AIforce delivery; ~10.5x NTM EPS ~$15 on ~$33B of net debt.

base.story: ~9-10% total growth (organic ~7-8% plus Contentful/Fin), ~34% non-GAAP margin, ASR lifts per-share growth; enterprise app demand holds as at Oracle (apps +10%) and ServiceNow; ~14.5x NTM core EPS ~$17.4.

bull.story: Organic growth reaccelerates to ~10%+ as Agentforce/Data 360 consumption revenue compounds and agentic spend (Gartner) accrues to the system of record; seat trends stay positive; multiple to ~18x NTM EPS ~$18. Any Anthropic stake monetization is upside optionality, not a driver.

thesis_break_reason: Below ~$163 (about 10x FY28 core EPS of ~$16.2, back in the June-2026 trough zone) the market would be pricing actual seat-base decline or a failed organic reacceleration (cRPO well below ~14%, FY28 guide under ~8%), i.e. the industry 'SaaSpocalypse' thesis winning rather than 45%-vol noise; it would also leave the $182-average ASR underwater on ~$39B of gross debt.

reasoning: Round 2. Industry lane: peers show AI expanding rather than killing incumbent application platforms in 2026 (ServiceNow +24%, HubSpot +20%, Oracle cloud apps +10% with Fusion +14% in Sep-2026), but pricing is moving from seat to meter/outcome (HubSpot, ServiceNow) and Microsoft says CRM bookings are moderating; IDC shows Salesforce holding ~20% share but slightly lagging the market. Supervisor corrections accepted after checking the primary 8-K exhibit: SBC is 9.0% of revenue (my round-1 ~7%/$3.3B was wrong), H1 gains were $2.98, post-ASR shares ~787M, net debt must include ~$5.1B of deal cash, and the $63B FY30 target includes M&A. Rebuilt: P/E 14.5x NTM $17.4 = $252; SBC-adjusted FCF 6.2% = $250; EV/sales 4.2x = $251; fair value $251 (from $262). I keep a slightly richer FCF yield (6.2% vs the supervisor's 6.4%) because of high FCF conversion and ongoing buybacks. Scenarios 158/250/325 at 25/50/25 give a mean ~$246. The ladder is a lognormal mixture (median ~$243, 85% sigma 0.36 / 15% sigma 0.60) with the upper tail trimmed per the supervisor (P>=405 0.108 -> 0.085, P>=578 0.017 -> 0.012) since the Anthropic-IPO bull driver is speculative. Research in round 2 was limited to a primary-filing check and two searches.
